newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Feb. 11.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Feb. 11.

text.p: Three Gulf of Mexico ports were reported closed Tuesday, two of which are key crude shipping ports, the Communications and Transport Ministry said in its 1000 local/1600 GMT daily report.

Crude ports Dos Bocas in Tabasco state and Pajaritos in Veracruz state were shut for exports. At Dos Bocas waves were reported at heights of between 10 and 12 feet, and at Pajaritos winds blew up to 40 km per hour.
The nation's largest crude port, Cayo Arcas, remained open amid moderate wind velocities.
Progreso port in Yucatan state was shut amid winds from the northeast at 44 km per hour and waves at eight feet high.
The ministry advised ships to exercise caution in the Gulf of Tehuantepec because of strong winds and high waves.
Smaller ships, such as fishing and tourism boats, were restricted from sailing at Salina Cruz, Veracruz, Alvarado and Nautla ports.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean and Pacific Coast.

Weak cold front hovering over northwest region of country causing winds of 15 to 20 knots (28 to 38 km/17 to 22 miles per hour) with waves of three to six feet high along coasts of Baja California, Sonora and Sinoloa states. Lighter winds along coast of Oaxaca state and rest of Pacific shores. -- Gulf of Mexico:

Cold air still in southeast gulf region, where light rains and clouds along Yucatan peninsula, with winds of 10 to 20 knots (19 to 38 km/11 to 22 miles per hour). Light drop in temperature also along north of gulf. -- Caribbean:
Cloudy with light rains along coasts of Quintana Roo and Central America with moderate winds at 20 to 30 km per hour.
